name: What Changed in the Contract?: Ladder
description: Ten levels of the same job: compare two drafts of a services agreement and list every substantive change by clause or schedule row in version 2, with its type and old and new values, while ignoring renumbering, moved clauses, re-sorted schedules and reformatted numbers. Level 1 is a short agreement with three changed values; every level adds length and kinds of edit (a "not" flipped, a clause added that renumbers a section, schedules, definitions, deleted and moved clauses, governing law, "shall" turned into "may", obligations moved to the other party, re-pointed cross-references); level 5 is the longest case of What Changed in the Contract?, and levels 6 to 10 grow to about 115 changes in two drafts of some 17,500 words with a fourth schedule, a second new section, re-sorted site and asset lists and up to fourteen subtle changes. Listing a non-change costs as much as missing a change; a level is passed at 90% of its points.
hook: From a one-page redline to two 9,000-word drafts: how far up can it climb without missing a change or inventing one?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
Our supplier has sent back a revised draft of our services agreement. Before I sign, tell me exactly what they changed.

List every SUBSTANTIVE change between version 1 and version 2 — a change that alters what either party must do, may do, pays or risks. Do NOT list changes that only affect presentation: clause or section renumbering, cross-references renumbered so they still point at the same clause, a clause moved somewhere else with the same words, the same number written differently ("thirty (30) days" / "30 days", "£250,000" / "£250,000.00", "5%" / "5 per cent"), headings, capitals or spelling. Listing a change that is not substantive costs as much as missing one.

For each substantive change give:
- the clause number in VERSION 2 (for a deleted clause, its number in version 1);
- type: one of "amount" (a sum of money), "percent", "number" (a count, e.g. visits a month), "days", "months", "years", "hours" (a time period in that unit), "governing_law", "negation" (a "not" added or removed, reversing the clause), "obligation" ("shall" changed to "may" or back), "party" (the obligation moved to the other party), "cross_reference" (a reference that now points at a DIFFERENT clause), "added" (a new clause or schedule row), "deleted" (a clause or row removed), "definition" (a change inside a definition in section 1);
- old and new: the old and new values for amount (in pounds), percent, number, days, months, years and hours (numbers only), for governing_law (the jurisdiction's name as written), for party ("Supplier" or "Customer") and for cross_reference (the clause number written in version 1 and the one written in version 2); null for negation, obligation, added, deleted and definition.
Schedule rows are numbered S1.1, S1.2, … (S2.x, S3.x for the later schedules) and count as clauses.
Only list a clause whose own wording changed (or that was added or removed); a clause whose words are unchanged is not listed even if a changed definition affects it.

SERVICES AGREEMENT between Pennine Dental Group Ltd (the Customer) and Corran Workplace Services Ltd (the Supplier) — version 2 (Supplier's revised draft)

1. Definitions
1.1 “Business Day” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England.
1.2 “Business Hours” means 08:30 to 17:00 on a Business Day.
1.3 “Charges” means the fees payable by the Customer under clause 8.1, exclusive of VAT.
1.4 “Confidential Information” means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement, whether in writing, orally or by any other means.
1.5 “Services” means the facilities management services described in this Agreement, delivered at the Sites listed in Schedule 1.

2. Social Value
2.1 The Supplier shall deliver the social value commitments in its tender, including apprenticeships and spending with local businesses, and report on them in each Contract Year.
2.2 The Supplier shall publish a social value statement within 90 days of the end of each Contract Year.

3. Term
3.1 This Agreement starts on the Commencement Date and continues for an initial term of 12 months (the “Initial Term”).
3.2 At the end of the Initial Term this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of 12 months unless either party gives the other written notice of at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
3.3 Unless renewed or terminated earlier under this Agreement, this Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term.

4. Supply of the Services
4.1 The Supplier shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with Good Industry Practice and with all applicable laws.
4.2 The Supplier may subcontract any part of the Services without the Customer’s prior written consent.
4.3 The Supplier shall ensure that all personnel engaged in the Services are suitably trained, supervised and security vetted.
4.4 The Supplier shall respond to every Priority 1 incident within 4 hours of the incident being reported to the helpdesk, counting Business Hours only.
4.5 The Supplier may keep complete and accurate records of the Services and of the Charges, and shall allow the Customer or its auditors to inspect them on reasonable notice during Business Hours.
4.6 While on any Site the Supplier’s personnel shall comply with the Customer’s health and safety rules and site security procedures as notified to the Supplier from time to time.

5. Assets and Equipment
5.1 The Supplier shall maintain the assets listed in Schedule 4 in accordance with clause 4.1 and the manufacturer’s instructions.
5.2 The Customer shall bear the cost of replacing any asset in Schedule 4 that reaches the end of its working life during the Term.
5.3 The Supplier may keep an up-to-date asset register for the Sites and give the Customer a copy on request.
5.4 The Supplier shall report any asset that fails a statutory inspection within 24 hours of the inspection.
5.5 The Supplier shall hold a stock of critical spare parts for the assets in Schedule 4 at its own cost.
5.6 Assets installed after the Commencement Date are added to Schedule 4 and maintained under clause 5.3 from the date of installation.

6. Service Levels
6.1 The helpdesk shall be available for at least 98.5 per cent of Business Hours in each calendar month.
6.2 If the Supplier misses a service level in any month, the Customer is entitled to a service credit of 10 per cent of that month’s Charges for each service level missed.
6.3 Service credits for any month shall not exceed 20 per cent of the Charges for that month, and are the Customer’s sole financial remedy for missed service levels.

7. Governance
7.1 The parties shall hold a contract review meeting each quarter to review performance against the service level set out in clause 6.3.
7.2 The Supplier shall deliver a monthly performance report on the matters set out in clause 6.2, no later than the tenth Business Day of the following month.
7.3 The Customer shall comment on each monthly performance report within 10 days of receiving it, failing which the report is treated as accepted.
7.4 A dispute that is not resolved at a contract review meeting may be referred by either party for resolution under clause 14.2.
7.5 The service level targets in Schedule 2 may be reviewed once in each Contract Year and changed only under clause 8.5.
7.6 If the Supplier is in material breach of clause 4.4, the Customer may step in and perform the affected Services itself or through a third party at the Supplier’s reasonable cost.
7.7 The Supplier shall prepare and circulate the minutes of each contract review meeting within five Business Days.

8. Charges and Payment
8.1 The Customer shall pay the Supplier a monthly fee of £8,450.00 for the Services.
8.2 The Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears, and the Customer shall pay each valid invoice within 45 days of receiving it.
8.3 The Customer shall be entitled to withhold payment of any amount that it disputes in good faith while the dispute is resolved.
8.4 Interest on late payments accrues daily at 8 per cent a year above the Bank of England base rate from the due date until payment.
8.5 The Supplier may increase the Charges once in each Contract Year by no more than 5 per cent, by giving the Customer written notice at least 60 days in advance.

9. Business Continuity
9.1 The Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services and test it at least once in each Contract Year.
9.2 If the plan is invoked, the Supplier shall restore the Services within 24 hours and shall keep the Customer informed of progress at least daily.

10. Insurance
10.1 The Customer shall maintain public liability insurance with a limit of at least £5,000,000.00 for any one claim.
10.2 The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of at least £1,000,000.00 in the aggregate.
10.3 On request, the Supplier may give the Customer evidence that the insurances required by this clause are in force.
10.4 The Supplier shall notify the Customer promptly of any event that may give rise to a claim under the insurances required by this clause, and of any cancellation or material change to those insurances.

11. Confidentiality
11.1 Each party shall keep the other’s Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement and disclose it only to those of its personnel who need to know it.
11.2 The obligations in clause 11.1 survive termination or expiry of this Agreement for 2 years.
11.3 The obligations in this clause do not apply to information that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, or that a party is required by law or by a regulator to disclose.

12. Data Protection
12.1 On termination the Supplier shall, at the Customer’s choice, return or securely delete all personal data processed on the Customer’s behalf, unless the law requires it to keep a copy.
12.2 Each party shall comply with the Data Protection Legislation in relation to any personal data processed under this Agreement.
12.3 The Supplier shall notify the Customer of any personal data breach without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of becoming aware of it.
12.4 The Supplier shall engage another processor without the Customer’s prior written authorisation and shall impose on any such processor the same data protection obligations as are set out in this clause.

13. Limitation of Liability
13.1 Subject to clause 13.3, each party’s total liability arising under or in connection with this Agreement in each Contract Year shall not exceed £150,000.00.
13.2 Subject to clause 13.3, neither party is liable for any loss of profit, loss of goodwill or indirect or consequential loss.
13.3 Nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes either party’s liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for any other liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

14. Termination
14.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving the other written notice of at least 180 days.
14.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within 21 days of being notified of it.
14.3 On termination or expiry the Supplier shall provide reasonable exit assistance for up to 6 months so that the Services can transfer to the Customer or a replacement organization.

15. Non-Solicitation

16. General
16.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand or by recorded post to the address set out in the Order Form; a notice by email is valid only if it is also sent by post.
16.2 Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.

16.6 A failure or delay by a party to exercise any right or remedy under this Agreement is not a waiver of that right or remedy, and a single or partial exercise does not prevent any further exercise.

cases.prompt:
Our supplier has sent back a revised draft of our services agreement. Before I sign, tell me exactly what they changed.

List every SUBSTANTIVE change between version 1 and version 2 — a change that alters what either party must do, may do, pays or risks. Do NOT list changes that only affect presentation: clause or section renumbering, cross-references renumbered so they still point at the same clause, a clause moved somewhere else with the same words, the same number written differently ("thirty (30) days" / "30 days", "£250,000" / "£250,000.00", "5%" / "5 per cent"), headings, capitals or spelling. Listing a change that is not substantive costs as much as missing one.

For each substantive change give:
- the clause number in VERSION 2 (for a deleted clause, its number in version 1);
- type: one of "amount" (a sum of money), "percent", "number" (a count, e.g. visits a month), "days", "months", "years", "hours" (a time period in that unit), "governing_law", "negation" (a "not" added or removed, reversing the clause), "obligation" ("shall" changed to "may" or back), "party" (the obligation moved to the other party), "cross_reference" (a reference that now points at a DIFFERENT clause), "added" (a new clause or schedule row), "deleted" (a clause or row removed), "definition" (a change inside a definition in section 1);
- old and new: the old and new values for amount (in pounds), percent, number, days, months, years and hours (numbers only), for governing_law (the jurisdiction's name as written), for party ("Supplier" or "Customer") and for cross_reference (the clause number written in version 1 and the one written in version 2); null for negation, obligation, added, deleted and definition.
Schedule rows are numbered S1.1, S1.2, … (S2.x, S3.x for the later schedules) and count as clauses.
Only list a clause whose own wording changed (or that was added or removed); a clause whose words are unchanged is not listed even if a changed definition affects it.

8.1 The Supplier shall maintain public liability insurance with a limit of at least £2,000,000 for any one claim.

SERVICES AGREEMENT between Larkspur Academy Trust (the Customer) and Kestrel Property Care Ltd (the Supplier) — version 2 (Supplier's revised draft)

1. Definitions
1.1 “Business Day” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Scotland.
1.2 “Business Hours” means 09:00 to 17:30 on a Business Day.
1.3 “Charges” means the fees payable by the Customer under clause 8.1, exclusive of VAT.
1.4 “Confidential Information” means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement, whether in writing, orally or by any other means.
1.5 “Services” means the facilities management services described in this Agreement, delivered at the Sites listed in Schedule 1.

2. Social Value
2.1 The Supplier shall deliver the social value commitments in its tender, including apprenticeships and spending with local businesses, and report on them in each Contract Year.
2.2 The Supplier shall publish a social value statement within 90 days of the end of each Contract Year.

3. Term
3.1 This Agreement starts on the Commencement Date and continues for an initial term of 36 months (the “Initial Term”).
3.2 At the end of the Initial Term this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of 12 months unless either party gives the other written notice of at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
3.3 Unless renewed or terminated earlier under this Agreement, this Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term.

4. Supply of the Services
4.1 The Supplier shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with Good Industry Practice and with all applicable laws.
4.2 The Supplier may not subcontract any part of the Services without the Customer’s prior written consent.
4.3 The Supplier shall ensure that all personnel engaged in the Services are suitably trained, supervised and security vetted.
4.4 The Supplier shall respond to every Priority 1 incident within 4 hours of the incident being reported to the helpdesk, counting Business Hours only.
4.5 The Supplier may keep complete and accurate records of the Services and of the Charges, and shall allow the Customer or its auditors to inspect them on reasonable notice during Business Hours.
4.6 While on any Site the Supplier’s personnel shall comply with the Customer’s health and safety rules and site security procedures as notified to the Supplier from time to time.

5. Assets and Equipment
5.1 The Supplier shall maintain the assets listed in Schedule 4 in accordance with clause 4.1 and the manufacturer’s instructions.
5.2 The Supplier shall bear the cost of replacing any asset in Schedule 4 that reaches the end of its working life during the Term.
5.3 The Supplier shall keep an up-to-date asset register for the Sites and give the Customer a copy on request.
5.4 The Supplier shall report any asset that fails a statutory inspection within 72 hours of the inspection.
5.5 The Supplier shall not hold a stock of critical spare parts for the assets in Schedule 4 at its own cost.
5.6 Assets installed after the Commencement Date are added to Schedule 4 and maintained under clause 5.3 from the date of installation.

6. Service Levels
6.1 The helpdesk shall be available for at least 99.5 per cent of Business Hours in each calendar month.
6.2 If the Supplier misses a service level in any month, the Customer is entitled to a service credit of 2.5 per cent of that month’s Charges for each service level missed.
6.3 Service credits for any month shall not exceed 20 per cent of the Charges for that month, and are the Customer’s sole financial remedy for missed service levels.

7. Governance
7.1 The parties shall hold a contract review meeting each quarter to review performance against the service level set out in clause 6.3.
7.2 The Supplier shall deliver a monthly performance report on the matters set out in clause 6.2, no later than the tenth Business Day of the following month.
7.3 The Customer shall comment on each monthly performance report within 20 days of receiving it, failing which the report is treated as accepted.
7.4 A dispute that is not resolved at a contract review meeting may be referred by either party for resolution under clause 14.1.
7.5 The service level targets in Schedule 2 may be reviewed once in each Contract Year and changed only under clause 8.5.
7.6 If the Supplier is in material breach of clause 4.4, the Customer may step in and perform the affected Services itself or through a third party at the Supplier’s reasonable cost.
7.7 The Customer shall prepare and circulate the minutes of each contract review meeting within five Business Days.

8. Charges and Payment
8.1 The Customer shall pay the Supplier a monthly fee of £8,450.00 for the Services.
8.2 The Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears, and the Customer shall pay each valid invoice within 30 days of receiving it.
8.3 The Customer shall be entitled to withhold payment of any amount that it disputes in good faith while the dispute is resolved.
8.4 Interest on late payments accrues daily at 3 per cent a year above the Bank of England base rate from the due date until payment.
8.5 The Supplier may increase the Charges once in each Contract Year by no more than 3 per cent, by giving the Customer written notice at least 60 days in advance.

9. Business Continuity
9.1 The Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services and test it at least once in each Contract Year.
9.2 If the plan is invoked, the Supplier shall restore the Services within 24 hours and shall keep the Customer informed of progress at least daily.

10. Insurance
10.1 The Supplier shall maintain public liability insurance with a limit of at least £10,000,000.00 for any one claim.
10.2 The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of at least £1,000,000.00 in the aggregate.
10.3 On request, the Supplier may give the Customer evidence that the insurances required by this clause are in force.
10.4 The Supplier shall notify the Customer promptly of any event that may give rise to a claim under the insurances required by this clause, and of any cancellation or material change to those insurances.

11. Confidentiality
11.1 Each party shall keep the other’s Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement and disclose it only to those of its personnel who need to know it.
11.2 The obligations in clause 11.1 survive termination or expiry of this Agreement for 2 years.
11.3 The obligations in this clause do not apply to information that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, or that a party is required by law or by a regulator to disclose.

12. Data Protection
12.1 Each party shall comply with the Data Protection Legislation in relation to any personal data processed under this Agreement.
12.2 The Supplier shall notify the Customer of any personal data breach without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.
12.3 The Supplier shall engage another processor without the Customer’s prior written authorisation and shall impose on any such processor the same data protection obligations as are set out in this clause.
12.4 On termination the Supplier shall, at the Customer’s choice, return or securely delete all personal data processed on the Customer’s behalf, unless the law requires it to keep a copy.

13. Limitation of Liability
13.1 Subject to clause 13.3, each party’s total liability arising under or in connection with this Agreement in each Contract Year shall not exceed £1,000,000.00.
13.2 Subject to clause 13.3, neither party is liable for any loss of profit, loss of goodwill or indirect or consequential loss.
13.3 Nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes either party’s liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for any other liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

14. Termination
14.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving the other written notice of at least 180 days.
14.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within 30 days of being notified of it.
14.3 On termination or expiry the Supplier shall provide reasonable exit assistance for up to 2 months so that the Services can transfer to the Customer or a replacement organization.

Our supplier has sent back a revised draft of our services agreement. Before I sign, tell me exactly what they changed.

List every SUBSTANTIVE change between version 1 and version 2 — a change that alters what either party must do, may do, pays or risks. Do NOT list changes that only affect presentation: clause or section renumbering, cross-references renumbered so they still point at the same clause, a clause moved somewhere else with the same words, the same number written differently ("thirty (30) days" / "30 days", "£250,000" / "£250,000.00", "5%" / "5 per cent"), headings, capitals or spelling. Listing a change that is not substantive costs as much as missing one.

For each substantive change give:
- the clause number in VERSION 2 (for a deleted clause, its number in version 1);
- type: one of "amount" (a sum of money), "percent", "number" (a count, e.g. visits a month), "days", "months", "years", "hours" (a time period in that unit), "governing_law", "negation" (a "not" added or removed, reversing the clause), "obligation" ("shall" changed to "may" or back), "party" (the obligation moved to the other party), "cross_reference" (a reference that now points at a DIFFERENT clause), "added" (a new clause or schedule row), "deleted" (a clause or row removed), "definition" (a change inside a definition in section 1);
- old and new: the old and new values for amount (in pounds), percent, number, days, months, years and hours (numbers only), for governing_law (the jurisdiction's name as written), for party ("Supplier" or "Customer") and for cross_reference (the clause number written in version 1 and the one written in version 2); null for negation, obligation, added, deleted and definition.
Schedule rows are numbered S1.1, S1.2, … (S2.x, S3.x for the later schedules) and count as clauses.
Only list a clause whose own wording changed (or that was added or removed); a clause whose words are unchanged is not listed even if a changed definition affects it.

SERVICES AGREEMENT between Larkspur Academy Trust (the Customer) and Kestrel Property Care Ltd (the Supplier) — version 1 (draft sent 9 June)

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 “Business Day” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England.
1.2 “Business Hours” means 09:00 to 17:30 on a Business Day.
1.3 “Charges” means the fees payable by the Customer under clause 7.1, exclusive of VAT.
1.4 “Confidential Information” means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement, whether in writing, orally or by any other means.
1.5 “Services” means the facilities management services described in this Agreement, delivered at the Sites listed in Schedule 1.

2. TERM
2.1 This Agreement starts on the Commencement Date and continues for an initial term of twelve (12) months (the “Initial Term”).
2.2 Unless renewed or terminated earlier under this Agreement, this Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term.

3. SUPPLY OF THE SERVICES
3.1 The Supplier shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with Good Industry Practice and with all applicable laws.
3.2 The Supplier may not subcontract any part of the Services without the Customer’s prior written consent.
3.3 The Supplier shall ensure that all personnel engaged in the Services are suitably trained, supervised and security vetted.
3.4 The Supplier shall respond to every Priority 1 incident within two (2) hours of the incident being reported to the helpdesk, counting Business Hours only.
3.5 The Supplier shall keep complete and accurate records of the Services and of the Charges, and shall allow the Customer or its auditors to inspect them on reasonable notice during Business Hours.
3.6 While on any Site the Supplier’s personnel shall comply with the Customer’s health and safety rules and site security procedures as notified to the Supplier from time to time.

4. ASSETS AND EQUIPMENT
4.1 The Supplier shall maintain the assets listed in Schedule 4 in accordance with clause 3.1 and the manufacturer’s instructions.
4.2 The Customer shall bear the cost of replacing any asset in Schedule 4 that reaches the end of its working life during the Term.
4.3 The Supplier shall keep an up-to-date asset register for the Sites and give the Customer a copy on request.
4.4 The Supplier shall report any asset that fails a statutory inspection within twenty-four (24) hours of the inspection.
4.5 The Supplier shall hold a stock of critical spare parts for the assets in Schedule 4 at its own cost.
4.6 Assets installed after the Commencement Date are added to Schedule 4 and maintained under clause 4.1 from the date of installation.

5. SERVICE LEVELS
5.1 The helpdesk shall be available for at least 99.5% of Business Hours in each calendar month.
5.2 If the Supplier misses a service level in any month, the Customer is entitled to a service credit of 2.5% of that month’s Charges for each service level missed.
5.3 Service credits for any month shall not exceed 15% of the Charges for that month, and are the Customer’s sole financial remedy for missed service levels.

6. GOVERNANCE
6.1 The parties shall hold a contract review meeting each quarter to review performance against the service level set out in clause 5.1.
6.2 The Supplier shall deliver a monthly performance report on the matters set out in clause 5.2, no later than the tenth Business Day of the following month.
6.3 The Customer shall comment on each monthly performance report within ten (10) days of receiving it, failing which the report is treated as accepted.
6.4 A dispute that is not resolved at a contract review meeting may be referred by either party for resolution under clause 12.2.
6.5 The service level targets in Schedule 2 may be reviewed once in each Contract Year and changed only under clause 14.9.
6.6 If the Supplier is in material breach of clause 3.1, the Customer may step in and perform the affected Services itself or through a third party at the Supplier’s reasonable cost.
6.7 The Supplier shall prepare and circulate the minutes of each contract review meeting within five Business Days.

7. CHARGES AND PAYMENT
7.1 The Customer shall pay the Supplier a monthly fee of £12,600 for the Services.
7.2 The Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears, and the Customer shall pay each valid invoice within sixty (60) days of receiving it.
7.3 The Customer shall be entitled to withhold payment of any amount that it disputes in good faith while the dispute is resolved.
7.4 Interest on late payments accrues daily at 4% a year above the Bank of England base rate from the due date until payment.
7.5 The Supplier may increase the Charges once in each Contract Year by no more than 7.5%, by giving the Customer written notice at least thirty (30) days in advance.

8. INSURANCE
8.1 The Supplier shall maintain public liability insurance with a limit of at least £10,000,000 for any one claim.
8.2 The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of at least £2,000,000 in the aggregate.
8.3 On request, the Supplier shall give the Customer evidence that the insurances required by this clause are in force.
8.4 The Supplier shall notify the Customer promptly of any event that may give rise to a claim under the insurances required by this clause, and of any cancellation or material change to those insurances.

9. CONFIDENTIALITY
9.1 Each party shall keep the other’s Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement and disclose it only to those of its personnel who need to know it.
9.2 The obligations in clause 9.1 survive termination or expiry of this Agreement for three (3) years.
9.3 The obligations in this clause do not apply to information that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, or that a party is required by law or by a regulator to disclose.

10. DATA PROTECTION
10.1 Each party shall comply with the Data Protection Legislation in relation to any personal data processed under this Agreement.
10.2 The Supplier shall notify the Customer of any personal data breach without undue delay and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of it.
10.3 The Supplier shall not engage another processor without the Customer’s prior written authorisation and shall impose on any such processor the same data protection obligations as are set out in this clause.
10.4 On termination the Supplier shall, at the Customer’s choice, return or securely delete all personal data processed on the Customer’s behalf, unless the law requires it to keep a copy.

11. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
11.1 Nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes either party’s liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for any other liability that cannot lawfully be limited.
11.2 Subject to clause 11.1, each party’s total liability arising under or in connection with this Agreement in each Contract Year shall not exceed £1,000,000.
11.3 Subject to clause 11.1, neither party is liable for any loss of profit, loss of goodwill or indirect or consequential loss.

12. TERMINATION
12.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving the other written notice of at least one hundred and eighty (180) days.
12.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within thirty (30) days of being notified of it.
12.3 On termination or expiry the Supplier shall provide reasonable exit assistance for up to three (3) months so that the Services can transfer to the Customer or a replacement organisation.
12.4 The parties shall cooperate in good faith on any transfer of employees that may occur on termination under the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006.

13. NON-SOLICITATION
13.1 Neither party shall, without the other’s consent, solicit or employ any person employed by the other in the delivery of the Services during this Agreement and for six (6) months after it ends.

14. GENERAL
14.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand or by recorded post to the address set out in the Order Form; a notice by email is valid only if it is also sent by post.
14.2 Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
14.3 This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all earlier discussions, proposals and agreements about its subject matter.
14.4 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.
14.5 Neither party is in breach of this Agreement or liable for any delay in performing its obligations if the delay results from events beyond its reasonable control, provided that it notifies the other promptly and uses reasonable endeavours to limit the effect of the event.
14.6 Each party shall comply with the Bribery Act 2010 and the Modern Slavery Act 2015 and shall maintain policies and procedures designed to ensure compliance.
14.7 A failure or delay by a party to exercise any right or remedy under this Agreement is not a waiver of that right or remedy, and a single or partial exercise does not prevent any further exercise.
14.8 If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid or unenforceable, it shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, and the rest of this Agreement is not affected.
14.9 No variation of this Agreement is effective unless it is in writing and signed by an authorised representative of each party.
14.10 A person who is not a party to this Agreement has no right under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 to enforce any of its terms.
14.11 This Agreement may be signed in any number of counterparts, each of which is an original and which together form one agreement.

SERVICES AGREEMENT between Larkspur Academy Trust (the Customer) and Kestrel Property Care Ltd (the Supplier) — version 2 (Supplier's revised draft)

1. Definitions
1.1 “Business Day” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Scotland.
1.2 “Business Hours” means 09:00 to 17:30 on a Business Day.
1.3 “Charges” means the fees payable by the Customer under clause 8.1, exclusive of VAT.
1.4 “Confidential Information” means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement, whether in writing, orally or by any other means.
1.5 “Services” means the facilities management services described in this Agreement, delivered at the Sites listed in Schedule 1.

2. Social Value
2.1 The Supplier shall deliver the social value commitments in its tender, including apprenticeships and spending with local businesses, and report on them in each Contract Year.
2.2 The Supplier shall publish a social value statement within 90 days of the end of each Contract Year.

3. Term
3.1 This Agreement starts on the Commencement Date and continues for an initial term of 24 months (the “Initial Term”).
3.2 At the end of the Initial Term this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of 12 months unless either party gives the other written notice of at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
3.3 Unless renewed or terminated earlier under this Agreement, this Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term.

4. Supply of the Services
4.1 While on any Site the Supplier’s personnel shall comply with the Customer’s health and safety rules and site security procedures as notified to the Supplier from time to time.
4.2 The Supplier shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with Good Industry Practice and with all applicable laws.
4.3 The Supplier may subcontract any part of the Services without the Customer’s prior written consent.
4.4 The Supplier shall ensure that all personnel engaged in the Services are suitably trained, supervised and security vetted.
4.5 The Supplier shall respond to every Priority 1 incident within 4 hours of the incident being reported to the helpdesk, counting Business Hours only.
4.6 The Supplier may keep complete and accurate records of the Services and of the Charges, and shall allow the Customer or its auditors to inspect them on reasonable notice during Business Hours.

5. Assets and Equipment
5.1 The Supplier shall maintain the assets listed in Schedule 4 in accordance with clause 4.4 and the manufacturer’s instructions.
5.2 The Supplier shall bear the cost of replacing any asset in Schedule 4 that reaches the end of its working life during the Term.
5.3 The Supplier may keep an up-to-date asset register for the Sites and give the Customer a copy on request.
5.4 The Supplier shall report any asset that fails a statutory inspection within 72 hours of the inspection.
5.5 The Supplier shall hold a stock of critical spare parts for the assets in Schedule 4 at its own cost.
5.6 Assets installed after the Commencement Date are added to Schedule 4 and maintained under clause 5.3 from the date of installation.

6. Service Levels
6.1 The helpdesk shall be available for at least 99 per cent of Business Hours in each calendar month.
6.2 If the Supplier misses a service level in any month, the Customer is entitled to a service credit of 10 per cent of that month’s Charges for each service level missed.
6.3 Service credits for any month shall not exceed 25 per cent of the Charges for that month, and are the Customer’s sole financial remedy for missed service levels.

7. Governance
7.1 The parties shall hold a contract review meeting each quarter to review performance against the service level set out in clause 6.3.
7.2 The Supplier shall deliver a monthly performance report on the matters set out in clause 6.1, no later than the tenth Business Day of the following month.
7.3 The Customer shall comment on each monthly performance report within 20 days of receiving it, failing which the report is treated as accepted.
7.4 A dispute that is not resolved at a contract review meeting may be referred by either party for resolution under clause 14.1.
7.5 The service level targets in Schedule 2 may be reviewed once in each Contract Year and changed only under clause 16.6.
7.6 If the Supplier is in material breach of clause 4.5, the Customer may step in and perform the affected Services itself or through a third party at the Supplier’s reasonable cost.
7.7 The Customer shall prepare and circulate the minutes of each contract review meeting within five Business Days.

8. Charges and Payment
8.1 The Customer shall pay the Supplier a monthly fee of £14,975.00 for the Services.
8.2 The Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears, and the Customer shall pay each valid invoice within 30 days of receiving it.
8.3 The Customer shall be entitled to withhold payment of any amount that it disputes in good faith while the dispute is resolved.
8.4 Interest on late payments accrues daily at 8 per cent a year above the Bank of England base rate from the due date until payment.
8.5 The Supplier may increase the Charges once in each Contract Year by no more than 7.5 per cent, by giving the Customer written notice at least 60 days in advance.

9. Business Continuity
9.1 The Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services and test it at least once in each Contract Year.
9.2 If the plan is invoked, the Supplier shall restore the Services within 24 hours and shall keep the Customer informed of progress at least daily.

10. Insurance
10.1 The Supplier shall maintain public liability insurance with a limit of at least £5,000,000.00 for any one claim.
10.2 The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of at least £1,000,000.00 in the aggregate.
10.3 On request, the Supplier may give the Customer evidence that the insurances required by this clause are in force.
10.4 The Supplier shall notify the Customer promptly of any event that may give rise to a claim under the insurances required by this clause, and of any cancellation or material change to those insurances.

11. Confidentiality
11.1 Each party shall keep the other’s Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement and disclose it only to those of its personnel who need to know it.
11.2 The obligations in clause 11.1 survive termination or expiry of this Agreement for 2 years.
11.3 The obligations in this clause do not apply to information that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, or that a party is required by law or by a regulator to disclose.

12. Data Protection
12.1 On termination the Supplier shall, at the Customer’s choice, return or securely delete all personal data processed on the Customer’s behalf, unless the law requires it to keep a copy.
12.2 Each party shall comply with the Data Protection Legislation in relation to any personal data processed under this Agreement.
12.3 The Supplier shall notify the Customer of any personal data breach without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.
12.4 The Supplier shall engage another processor without the Customer’s prior written authorisation and shall impose on any such processor the same data protection obligations as are set out in this clause.

13. Limitation of Liability
13.1 Subject to clause 13.3, each party’s total liability arising under or in connection with this Agreement in each Contract Year shall not exceed £500,000.00.
13.2 Subject to clause 13.3, neither party is liable for any loss of profit, loss of goodwill or indirect or consequential loss.
13.3 Nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes either party’s liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for any other liability that cannot lawfully be limited.

14. Termination
14.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving the other written notice of at least 60 days.
14.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within 30 days of being notified of it.
14.3 On termination or expiry the Supplier shall provide reasonable exit assistance for up to 2 months so that the Services can transfer to the Customer or a replacement organization.
14.4 The parties shall cooperate in good faith on any transfer of employees that may occur on termination under the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006.

15. Non-Solicitation
15.1 Neither party shall, without the other’s consent, solicit or employ any person employed by the other in the delivery of the Services during this Agreement and for 12 months after it ends.

16. General
16.1 Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
16.2 This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all earlier discussions, proposals and agreements about its subject matter.
16.3 This Agreement and any dispute arising out of or in connection with it are governed by the law of Scotland, and the courts of Scotland have exclusive jurisdiction.
16.4 A failure or delay by a party to exercise any right or remedy under this Agreement is not a waiver of that right or remedy, and a single or partial exercise does not prevent any further exercise.
16.5 If any provision of this Agreement is found to be invalid or unenforceable, it shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, and the rest of this Agreement is not affected.
16.6 No variation of this Agreement is effective unless it is in writing and signed by an authorised representative of each party.
16.7 A person who is not a party to this Agreement has no right under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 to enforce any of its terms.
16.8 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand or by recorded post to the address set out in the Order Form; a notice by email is valid only if it is also sent by post.

1. Definitions
1.1 “Business Day” means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England.
1.2 “Business Hours” means 09:00 to 17:00 on a Business Day.
1.3 “Charges” means the fees payable by the Customer under clause 8.1, exclusive of VAT.
1.4 “Confidential Information” means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement, whether in writing, orally or by any other means.
1.5 “Services” means the facilities management services described in this Agreement, delivered at the Sites listed in Schedule 1.

2. Social Value
2.1 The Supplier shall deliver the social value commitments in its tender, including apprenticeships and spending with local businesses, and report on them in each Contract Year.
2.2 The Supplier shall publish a social value statement within 90 days of the end of each Contract Year.

3. Term
3.1 This Agreement starts on the Commencement Date and continues for an initial term of 12 months (the “Initial Term”).
3.2 At the end of the Initial Term this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods of 12 months unless either party gives the other written notice of at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
3.3 Unless renewed or terminated earlier under this Agreement, this Agreement expires at the end of the Initial Term.

4. Supply of the Services
4.1 While on any Site the Supplier’s personnel shall comply with the Customer’s health and safety rules and site security procedures as notified to the Supplier from time to time.
4.2 The Supplier shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with Good Industry Practice and with all applicable laws.
4.3 The Supplier may not subcontract any part of the Services without the Customer’s prior written consent.
4.4 The Supplier shall ensure that all personnel engaged in the Services are suitably trained, supervised and security vetted.
4.5 The Supplier shall respond to every Priority 1 incident within 2 hours of the incident being reported to the helpdesk, counting Business Hours only.
4.6 The Supplier may keep complete and accurate records of the Services and of the Charges, and shall allow the Customer or its auditors to inspect them on reasonable notice during Business Hours.

5. Assets and Equipment
5.1 The Supplier shall maintain the assets listed in Schedule 4 in accordance with clause 4.4 and the manufacturer’s instructions.
5.2 The Supplier shall bear the cost of replacing any asset in Schedule 4 that reaches the end of its working life during the Term.
5.3 The Supplier may keep an up-to-date asset register for the Sites and give the Customer a copy on request.
5.4 The Supplier shall report any asset that fails a statutory inspection within 48 hours of the inspection.
5.5 The Supplier shall not hold a stock of critical spare parts for the assets in Schedule 4 at its own cost.
5.6 Assets installed after the Commencement Date are added to Schedule 4 and maintained under clause 5.3 from the date of installation.

6. Service Levels
6.1 The helpdesk shall be available for at least 99.5 per cent of Business Hours in each calendar month.
6.2 If the Supplier misses a service level in any month, the Customer is entitled to a service credit of 10 per cent of that month’s Charges for each service level missed.
6.3 Service credits for any month shall not exceed 15 per cent of the Charges for that month, and are the Customer’s sole financial remedy for missed service levels.

7. Governance
7.1 The parties shall hold a contract review meeting each quarter to review performance against the service level set out in clause 6.3.
7.2 The Supplier shall deliver a monthly performance report on the matters set out in clause 6.1, no later than the tenth Business Day of the following month.
7.3 The Customer shall comment on each monthly performance report within 20 days of receiving it, failing which the report is treated as accepted.
7.4 A dispute that is not resolved at a contract review meeting may be referred by either party for resolution under clause 14.1.
7.5 The service level targets in Schedule 2 may be reviewed once in each Contract Year and changed only under clause 8.5.
7.6 If the Supplier is in material breach of clause 4.5, the Customer may step in and perform the affected Services itself or through a third party at the Supplier’s reasonable cost.
7.7 The Customer shall prepare and circulate the minutes of each contract review meeting within five Business Days.

8. Charges and Payment
8.1 The Customer shall pay the Supplier a monthly fee of £14,975.00 for the Services.
8.2 The Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears, and the Customer shall pay each valid invoice within 45 days of receiving it.
8.3 The Customer shall be entitled to withhold payment of any amount that it disputes in good faith while the dispute is resolved.
8.4 Interest on late payments accrues daily at 8 per cent a year above the Bank of England base rate from the due date until payment.
8.5 The Supplier may increase the Charges once in each Contract Year by no more than 3 per cent, by giving the Customer written notice at least 60 days in advance.

9. Business Continuity
9.1 The Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services and test it at least once in each Contract Year.
9.2 If the plan is invoked, the Supplier shall restore the Services within 24 hours and shall keep the Customer informed of progress at least daily.

10. Insurance
10.1 The Supplier shall maintain public liability insurance with a limit of at least £10,000,000.00 for any one claim.
10.2 The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of at least £1,000,000.00 in the aggregate.
10.3 On request, the Supplier may give the Customer evidence that the insurances required by this clause are in force.
10.4 The Supplier shall notify the Customer promptly of any event that may give rise to a claim under the insurances required by this clause, and of any cancellation or material change to those insurances.

11. Confidentiality
11.1 The obligations in this clause do not apply to information that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, or that a party is required by law or by a regulator to disclose.
11.2 Each party shall keep the other’s Confidential Information confidential, use it only to perform this Agreement and disclose it only to those of its personnel who need to know it.
11.3 The obligations in clause 11.2 survive termination or expiry of this Agreement for 5 years.

12. Data Protection
12.1 On termination the Supplier shall, at the Customer’s choice, return or securely delete all personal data processed on the Customer’s behalf, unless the law requires it to keep a copy.
12.2 Each party shall comply with the Data Protection Legislation in relation to any personal data processed under this Agreement.
12.3 The Supplier shall notify the Customer of any personal data breach without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.
12.4 The Supplier shall engage another processor without the Customer’s prior written authorisation and shall impose on any such processor the same data protection obligations as are set out in this clause.

13. Limitation of Liability
13.1 Subject to clause 13.3, each party’s total liability arising under or in connection with this Agreement in each Contract Year shall not exceed £1,000,000.00.
13.2 Subject to clause 13.3, neither party is liable for any loss of profit, loss of goodwill or indirect or consequential loss.

14. Termination
14.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving the other written notice of at least 180 days.
14.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within 21 days of being notified of it.
14.3 On termination or expiry the Supplier shall provide reasonable exit assistance for up to 2 months so that the Services can transfer to the Customer or a replacement organization.
14.4 The parties shall cooperate in good faith on any transfer of employees that may occur on termination under the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006.

15. Non-Solicitation
15.1 Neither party shall, without the other’s consent, solicit or employ any person employed by the other in the delivery of the Services during this Agreement and for 6 months after it ends.

16. General
16.1 Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld.
16.2 This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all earlier discussions, proposals and agreements about its subject matter.

16.4 A failure or delay by a party to exercise any right or remedy under this Agreement is not a waiver of that right or remedy, and a single or partial exercise does not prevent any further exercise.

16.6 This Agreement may be signed in any number of counterparts, each of which is an original and which together form one agreement.
